text:
Isabel Cruz: hi team - I think my relocation bonus was taxed by both UK PAYE and US federal this pay period. moved to London 04/20, bonus paid 04/25, but stub shows both withholdings. can someone confirm?

Connor (People Ops): sorry to hear that. can you paste the redacted paystub lines and confirm when you updated your address/residency?

Isabel Cruz: redacted lines: 
```
Pay date: 04/25
Payment: Relocation bonus GBP 4,000 (converted $5,200)
Deductions:
 - UK PAYE Income Tax: GBP 800 (applied by UK payroll partner)
 - US Federal Income Tax: $1,040 (applied by Redwood payroll)
Net received (after both taxes): approx $3,360
```
I filled out the move paperwork on 04/18 and updated my profile on 04/19. expected UK withholding only.

Payroll Bot: Auto: payrun pr-100112 completed. Notes: equity/bonus pipeline showed payment routed to intl_payroll adapter for UK partner, but Redwood domestic payroll also included a supplemental bonus tax event for employee id RED-9210 due to payment schedule entry. Duplicate taxation flagged: intl_payroll:PAYE and domestic:supplemental_fed both true. Mapping: payment_metadata.origin=relocation_bonus triggered both adapters.

Marta - Payroll: thanks Isabel. looks like a pipeline race where payroll created domestic supplemental tax on bonus when it saw a bonus record; concurrently an intl_payroll job also processed the same payment because finance requested gross-to-local conversion for partner. Essentially two systems each assumed responsibility and withheld. We'll need to reverse the domestic federal withholding (or request partner to refund UK PAYE) depending on which jurisdiction is correct. Given you're resident in UK and HR docs show move before payment, UK should be primary.

Ethan (Tax): tax view: for cross-border moves, primary taxing jurisdiction depends on residency and place of employment; if Isabel is UK tax resident and work performed in UK on pay date, employer should not withhold US federal on that compensation. Remediation: employer can refund US federal withholding via off-cycle payroll and then file corrected Employer Forms (941-X) for the quarter; we must also confirm HMRC treatment — partner should be asked to retain PAYE or refund depending on partner's policy. We should prioritize employee cash refund first.

Isabel Cruz: timeline? I need the net amount to cover moving costs.

Connor (People Ops): Marta - can payroll run an off-cycle to refund the US federal withholding and attach audit notes linking to intl_payrun? Also escalate to Finance to talk to UK partner about PAYE handling and to avoid duplicate in future.

Marta - Payroll: I will own the off-cycle. Drafting reversal now. Also opening a mapping fix: payment_metadata.origin should only be routed to a single tax adapter when payment has resident_country set. We will add a guard to the routing layer to avoid double-processing when intl_payroll partner confirms acceptance.

Payroll Bot: queued off-cycle pr-100112-refund for ts=1999991600.

Marta - Payroll: draft stub pre-run: 
```
Reversal: Domestic_Supplemental_Fed -$1,040.00
Off-cycle Refund: Refund_US_Fed $1,040.00
Notes: refund for duplicate US withholding on relocation bonus; audit ref pr-100112 -> pr-100112-refund.
```

Ethan (Tax): I'll prepare 941-X worksheet and calculation of employer deposit impact. If we reclaimed US deposit, we'll adjust ledgers and document for W-2 reconciliation. Also will draft communication for HMRC/UK partner if refund from partner required.

Payroll Bot: off-cycle job pr-100112-refund executed at ts=1999991700: SUCCESS. ACH refund initiated.

Isabel Cruz: saw pending refund in my account portal, thank you. Will this change my year-to-date tax totals and necessitate a corrected W-2 or P60/Treaty docs?

Ethan (Tax): Year-to-date payroll ledger will reflect the reversal; for US filings we'll consider 941-X if deposits already transmitted. For year-end forms: US W-2 should reflect corrected totals; if original W-2 was already issued, we'll prepare W-2c. For UK, partner will issue P60 equivalent; we'll coordinate so total gross matches across jurisdictions. We'll open ticket TAX-2026-UK-12 to track both HMRC partner reconciliation and W-2/W-2c decisions.

Connor (People Ops): root cause action: routing layer patch to prefer intl partner when resident_country present, add end-to-end test for relocation bonuses and add a pre-send hook to lock payment to single processor. Marta - please attach logs and partner receipt to audit.

Marta - Payroll: mapping fix committed (PR#pay-4509). Added pre-send lock. Also attached audit evidence: partner acceptance receipt and domestic supplemental tax event. Off-cycle refund completes at 1999991700.

Payroll Bot: Audit trail: pr-100112 -> pr-100112-refund. Mapping PR pay-4509 added unit/integration tests.

Isabel Cruz: thank you all 60a appreciate the quick coordination.

Ethan (Tax): created TAX-2026-UK-12 for follow-up on HMRC/partner reconciliation and W-2/W-2c impact.

Connor (People Ops): closing once TAX-2026-UK-12 created and refund clears. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
